lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Robert! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Kind of down this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, not much. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, finding the time makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I just forgot.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once the routine broke, it was easy to lose track.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I just forgot.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Dinner's late at your house.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Does your family eat salad?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The days got away from you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Frozen vegetables count just as much as fresh, and they're cheaper.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 5 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If finding the time gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: finding the time made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 5 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Marisol. Bye!

tags.note: Mood cue: 'kind of down' not explored

flags.reason: Participant said 'kind of down this week'; coach moved on without checking mood or wellbeing. Not an urgent safety signal, but worth a follow-up check.

Coach asked whether 5 days is realistic, then the participant voiced doubt and walking/knee barriers. The goal was set quickly with limited exploration of the participant's own confidence and preferences.

score.summary: The coach used good complex reflections of ambivalence (lines 10 and 33) and planned for barriers with an open backup-plan question (line 43). However, the participant's low mood at line 4 was not explored, and the coach moved quickly to a 5-day goal despite the participant's doubts.
strengths: Complex reflection of ambivalence at line 10 ('On one hand... On the other hand').
Open backup-plan question at line 43 supports barrier planning.
Clear summary and next-contact setting at lines 45 and 47.
coaching_tips: At line 4, follow up on 'kind of down' with an open question (e.g., 'What's been making this week feel down?') before moving to goals.
At line 21, ask what goal size feels right to Robert rather than testing realism, to strengthen partnership.
Ask permission before offering suggestions (as at line 35 ) and consider eliciting Robert's own ideas first next time.
